name: chip-families-from-datasheets
prompt: build me parameterized component families from these two datasheets — a chip resistor family and an MLCC family, no parts DB, the class should be the data so I can ask for any part in the catalog and get an orderable MPN back

inputs.notes:
Synthetic datasheets from the fictional ACME Passive Components house, matching the fictional-manufacturer convention the substrate-modeler's fab-report fixture uses. Synthetic because the real task fetches manufacturer PDFs at run time under a 'link the URL, don't commit the PDF' rule: a URL-only fixture cannot anchor a receipt lineage (a datasheet revision silently changes the input while compare still prints a delta), and committing real vendors' tables into a shipped bundle is a different redistribution posture from the derived dicts a component model holds.

The dimension tables are the physically standard EIA chip geometries, which is what makes the traps fire against a real library. Planted deliberately: APR 2512's T1 disagrees with the installed SMT_CHIP_DEFS entry and is the ONLY size that does; a size whose vendor label does not match its metric body (ACME '0075' is 0.30 x 0.15 mm, standard key '009005'); an NRFND size (1218); cross-axis restrictions (TCR M only on some sizes and only with tolerance D/F, packaging E only on the four largest, X5R absent from the 02 case); and an ordering example whose value carries a decade on rounding (9.995 kOhm -> 1002). The part-number grammar, code tables and lifecycle flags are invented; the geometry is not.

Not tested here: PDF page extraction via scripts/extract_pages.py, which a markdown fixture bypasses — the lm1117mp-son8-thermal-pad case carries that path. Two families rather than four; a third resistor vendor costs runner budget and adds no trap.

UPGRADE WATCH: the 2512 trap is version-dependent. jitxlib's corrected table gives 2512 lead_length 0.6 +/- 0.2 (matching this fixture, so the termination trap goes quiet) and body 6.3 +/- 0.2 x 3.15 +/- 0.15 (where this fixture prints 6.35 x 3.20, so an unintended body-dimension trap appears); the metric alias becomes 6332m. When the corrected table reaches the installed version, re-derive this fixture's 2512 row from it and move the deliberate single-size disagreement to an entry that is still genuinely wrong. Do not delete the assertion — the behaviour under test is that a candidate CHECKS the table, which holds whichever way it goes.

reference.notes: Verbatim copies of a shipped reference solution's shared chip helpers plus three of its families, kept as a package rather than flattened into one file — each family module defines its own module-level _build_mpn and code tables, so concatenating them into a single namespace would silently bind every class to the last family's helpers. IMPORTANT for judges: the reference is built from REAL vendor datasheets while the fixtures are the synthetic ACME analogues. Verify the candidate against the fixtures first — the reference shows one known-good shape (the shared/never-shared helper split, a standard-table override scoped to the single disagreeing size and pinned by a test that fails once jitxlib is corrected, a noise-free compact-value helper wrapping to_compact, insert parity with jitxlib.parts.Resistor), never the expected part numbers, packaging codes or size labels. Do not mark a candidate down for failing to match a real vendor's grammar. Keep runner directories free of this file.

runner_rationale: Customers drive this skill with mixed-strength agents. The skill must carry the goodness checks itself, so the eval runs the skill under a Sonnet-class runner rather than the strongest available model. Judges stay frontier-tier regardless of runner.
runner_isolation: Start the runner in a scratch directory with the skill, the fixtures and a writable output directory, and nothing else — no access to a repository containing a shipped solution of this shape. Reading the installed jitx/jitxlib API is expected; reading somebody's finished families measures the runner's search, not the skill. The reference under evals/cases/reference/ is for judges only.
runner_artifacts: The runner MUST write its completion summary to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only into its final chat message. Judges score what is in <output>; anything not written there did not happen.
runner_build: Tell the runner to run `jitx find` and build whatever target it prints, recording the exact command and result. Do NOT tell it to skip the build — the contract hard-fails on an available build that was not done, so forbidding it makes the run unwinnable. Where the build genuinely cannot run, the runner declares it as an open item in COMPLETION.md, which satisfies the hard-fail's own escape clause; remind judges that a declared, unavailable build is not a silent skip.
expected_output: A components/ package plus tests/ in which: one jitx.Component subclass covers each family, built in __init__ from fixture tables with no parts-DB or online query; shared vendor-agnostic helpers (chip dimensions, chip SMT land-pattern builder, two-pin insert, carry-correct significant rounding, a noise-free compact value helper) were extracted only once the second family landed and carry a component-agnostic name once a non-resistor family uses them; the per-vendor value encoder, size/rating tables and part-number grammar stay unshared; the land-pattern lead length comes from the band the outline dimensions on the seating plane (APR T1, ACC BW) and never the other one; the family that takes the generator's standard chip dimensions still transcribes the datasheet table and asserts the standard table against it per size, overriding only 2512 with a comment and a test that fails once jitxlib is fixed; every value encoder rounds before encoding so decade carries propagate; validation fails fast on every axis AND on the fixture's cross-axis restrictions, with messages listing the valid options; the MLCC's unpublished per-case capacitance lineup is documented as a gap with the ordering code and significand grid validated instead, rather than invented; tests subclass jitx.test.TestCase, build the parts in a SampleDesign, cross-check every worked ordering example from both fixtures, assert the human-readable value label, unit-test the encoders including the decade-carry cases, and assert validation raises; and the completion summary carries the filled Component completeness check block.

assertions.text: the full generated test suite passes
every generated source file parses as Python
generated files type-check (precondition: the runner project seeded pyright as a dev dependency)
every complete ordering example printed in either fixture is cross-checked somewhere in the generated tests
assertions.cmd: for m in $(grep -hoE '`(APR-[0-9A-Z-]+|ACC[0-9A-Z]+)`' evals/cases/fixtures/ACME-*.md | tr -d '`' | sort -u); do grep -rq "$m" <output> || { echo "ordering example not cross-checked: $m"; exit 1; }; done

assertions.text: a library-default guard test exists and passes — pytest exits 5 (no tests collected) if the runner never wrote one, which is how the 2512 termination band is caught
assertions.cmd: cd <output> && python3 -m pytest -q -k 'standard_table or termination or chip_def or smt_table'

assertions.text: no component is constructed inside a plain unittest.TestCase — outside the JITX instantiation context __init__ never runs, so such a test asserts nothing. Validation moved into a pure classmethod and tested plainly is a legitimate design and is NOT a finding; the rule is about construction, not the base class
a value-label test exists and passes, and no binary-float-noise magnitude was baked in as a numeric literal (a comment or docstring describing the hazard is not a finding)
assertions.cmd: cd <output> && python3 -m pytest -q -k 'value_label or label or renders' && python3 <skill>/evals/checks/float_noise.py <output>

assertions.text: density level is addressed, not silently defaulted — the resistor fixture asks for IPC-7351 nominal (DensityLevel.B) and JITX's global default is DensityLevel.C (IPC least), so the code must either set it explicitly or say in the completeness block why the default stands
the completion block was written to <output>/COMPLETION.md, not only reported in chat
the 2512 land pattern is not built from the standard table's 2.0 mm termination band — the realized pad extent along the part axis must reflect the fixture's 0.60 mm band

the band placed in the land pattern's lead length is the one each fixture dimensions on the seating plane (APR T1, ACC BW) and not the end-face band (T2, BE), the code says which and why, and the choice is cross-checked numerically across the two fixtures rather than guessed

the standard-table override is derived from the fixture, scoped to the single size that disagrees, commented with the magnitude of the error, and pinned by a test that FAILS once jitxlib is corrected — so the workaround is removed rather than left to rot
the 0075 case is matched to the standard table by body dimensions (0.30 x 0.15 mm -> key 009005) rather than by its vendor label, and the mapping is legible in the code

shared helpers were extracted when the second family landed and not before, carry a component-agnostic name once the capacitor family uses them, and the shared/never-shared split (geometry, insert, rounding shared; value encoder, part-number grammar, per-size tables not) matches what the two fixtures actually differ on
no invented numbers: spot-trace 10 values from the generated files back to fixture rows, including at least one per-size power rating, one packaging code, and the NRFND size's treatment

cross-axis restrictions are validated, not just per-axis ones — TCR M only on the sizes that offer it and only with tolerance D or F, packaging E only on the four largest cases, X5R absent from the 02 case — and every fail-fast message lists the valid options rather than only raising
the MLCC's unpublished per-case capacitance lineup is documented as a gap, with the ordering code and the class-I/class-II significand grids validated instead of a range being invented
the completion summary contains the filled Component completeness check block

future_cases: Planned: promote the markdown fixtures to a generated PDF so the extract_pages.py path is under test on a redistributable input; a fixture publishing no dimension table at all, where taking the generator defaults and saying so is correct; a third family in a component type with a different symbol class; and a dry-build assertion via jitx.run.discover.DryRunBuilder, which translates in-process when the CLI scanner cannot find a packaged layout.
